subject: Promotion of scalars to length-1 vectors in nimbleCode

messages.author: afbb7dae7cf4228f
messages.subject: Promotion of scalars to length-1 vectors in nimbleCode
parts:
Dear All,

This is a probably a really simple query but one that I seem to be having difficulty with.  I have written a custom distribution for NIMBLE that takes a vector is one of its arguments.  It is often used in the model specification in a similar way to this:

nimbleCode({
   # Prior on the scalar parameter
   myScalarParameter ~ dnorm(0.0, 0.001)
   # Use the parameter and a covariate to make an input argument for the distribution
   myInputArgument[1:numData] <- myScalarParameter * myCovariate[1:numData]
   # Likelihood calculation
   myData[1:numData] ~ dMyCustomDistribution(myInputArgument[1:numData])
})

However, in some cases, it will be more natural to provide a scalar argument here because, in many of our applications, this argument will not vary.  It would be nice to be able to write something like the following in the model specification:

nimbleCode({
    # Prior on the scalar parameter
    myScalarParameter ~ dnorm(0.0, 0.001)
    # Likelihood calculation
    myData[1:numData] ~ dMyCustomDistribution(myScalarParameter)
})

When I do this NIMBLE obviously complains that myScalarParameter is not a vector (which it isn't).  So, simple question: what is the best way to promote myScalarParameter to a 1-length vector (my custom function recycles the input vector to get an input vector of the right length)?

I've tried the following solutions but none of these seem to work:

nimbleCode({
   myScalarParameter[1] ~ dnorm(0.0, 0.001)
   myData[1:numData] ~ dMyCustomDistribution(myScalarParameter)
})
nimbleCode({
   myScalarParameter ~ dnorm(0.0, 0.001)
   myData[1:numData] ~ dMyCustomDistribution(c(myScalarParameter))
})

This seems to work but seems... clunky.

nimbleCode({
   # Prior on the scalar parameter
   myScalarParameter ~ dnorm(0.0, 0.001)
   # Make a vectorised version of the parameter
   for(dataIter in 1:numData) {
      myVectorisedParameter[dataIter] <- myScalarParameter
   }
   # Likelihood calculation
   myData[1:numData] ~ dMyCustomDistribution(myVectorisedParameter[1:numData])
})

I could of course make another custom distribution for the use of scalar arguments but that also would result in lots of annoying code replication and seems inelegant.

I'm just wondering if I'm missing something obvious.  I can provide the specific code for my case if that helps but I think my question here is more conceptual than implementation-specific.

Thank you in advance for any help you can provide.

All the best,

Joe

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Promotion of scalars to length-1 vectors in nimbleCode
parts:
Joe, NIMBLE can certainly handle this, and I'm sure we can figure it out.

In running the "second code box" that you provided, with the line:
myData[1:numData] ~ dMyCustomDistribution(myScalarParameter),

when you define the dMyCustomDistribution function as a nimbleFunction, do you specify that the argument should be of type double(), that is, to indicate it's going to be a scalar.  Meaning, for that to run, the definition should look like:

dMyCustomDistribution <- nimbleFunction(
   run = function(arg = double()) {
     .....
   }
)

If that's not the case, then it should be written that way, so it expects a scalar argument, and I think it would run fine.  If you're already doing that, and still getting an error about "myScalarParameter" not being a vector, then we'll have to look further.

Another cause could be if you're correctly defining the argument to be a scalar, but then using it as a vector inside dMyCustomDistribution.  That would be a problem.  For example:

dMyCustomDistribution <- nimbleFunction(
   run = function(arg = double()) {
     .....
     ..... <- arg[i]           ## using it as a vector.  This will cause an error.
   }
)

I'm sure we can figure this out.

parts:
Hi Daniel,

Thank you very much for your help.

You're right that, in our current implementation, our definition of the nimbleFunction is of the kind:

nimbleFunction(
   run = function(inputArg = double(1) {
      # My function's run code....
   }
)

That works OK for our vector example (in the first code box of the origional post) and, for exactly the reasons you specified doesn't work when inputArg is scalar as expected.

However, what we're trying to do is produce a library of custom distributions that will be useful both to our research but maybe others too.  In these cases it'd be nice for users of the distribution to be able to provide either vector or scalar input (as there are situations that might require use of either form).

Now we could make two custom distributions, one handling scalar input and one handling vector input of the form:

# Vector-input version
dmyDistribution_Vector <- nimbleFunciton(
   run = function(inputArg = double(1) {
       # Run processing of vector input...
   }
)

# Scalar-input version
dmyDistribution_Scalar <- nimbleFunction(
   run = function(inputArg = double() {
       # Create a vector version of the input argument ('myLength' could come from somewhere else like another argument
       inputArgVec <- numeric(value = inputArg, length = myLength, recycle = TRUE)
       # Run the vectorised version of the function
       return(dmyDistribution_Vector(inputArgVec))
   }
)

But that means that the users of the libraries will have two functions that do basically the same thing and that doesn't seem ideal from a design perspective.

Ideally we would just have the vectorised version defined as a distribution and then there be another function to 'promote' a scalar to a length-1 vector to be used in the model specification code for when users want to do this.  Something of the form:

nimbleCode({
   # Prior on the scalar parameter

myScalarParameter ~ dnorm(0.0, 0.001)
    # Likelihood calculation

myData[1:numData] ~ dMyCustomDistribution(promoteScalarToVec(myScalarParameter))
})

However, I'm not really sure of the cleanest way to do this in code that can be used in the model specification and my attempts to do so in code box 3 of the orginal post just gives me errors.

The code in box 4 works but creates an extra set of logical nodes in the model and slows things down quite a bit which is a bit of pain.  I could also write a custom 'promoteScalarToVec' function but that seems like something that should already exist.  I'm probably overlooking something really obvious.

Thanks again for all your help!

Joe

messages.subject: Re: Promotion of scalars to length-1 vectors in nimbleCode
parts:
Hi Joe,

Thanks for this question.

Unfortunately, there are a variety of corners where nimble's hard typing creates limitations, and this is one of them.  It's something we hope to improve in a deeper renovation, although maybe we should try to do something superficial faster.

One possible workaround would be to always make the argument to dMyCustomDistribution be a vector by padding it with a dummy value if necessary.  E.g. 

myParameter[1] <- whatever_you_really_need
myParameter[2] <- 0 ## a dummy to make myParameter a true vector.

Then when you call dMyCustomDistribution, you could include an additional argument indicating whether myParameter is padded in this way.

Oh no, I just noticed that in the newly released nimble 0.6-12, there is a bug in the automatic creation of "r" functions for custom distributions (when the user doesn't provide the "r" function).  We added a new error trap for missing return() statements, and the dummy version of the "r" function now errors out for this reason.  Evidently we don't have that case in our test suite.  I'll go post an issue on github.

Perry

   # Use the parameter and a covariate to make an input argument for the distribution
   myInputArgument[1:numData] <- myScalarParameter * myCovariate[1:numData]
   # Likelihood calculation
   myData[1:numData] ~ dMyCustomDistribution(myInputArgument[1:numData])
})

However, in some cases, it will be more natural to provide a scalar argument here because, in many of our applications, this argument will not vary.  It would be nice to be able to write something like the following in the model specification:

nimbleCode({
    # Prior on the scalar parameter
    myScalarParameter ~ dnorm(0.0, 0.001)
    # Likelihood calculation
    myData[1:numData] ~ dMyCustomDistribution(myScalarParameter)
})

When I do this NIMBLE obviously complains that myScalarParameter is not a vector (which it isn't).  So, simple question: what is the best way to promote myScalarParameter to a 1-length vector (my custom function recycles the input vector to get an input vector of the right length)?

I've tried the following solutions but none of these seem to work:

nimbleCode({
   myScalarParameter[1] ~ dnorm(0.0, 0.001)
   myData[1:numData] ~ dMyCustomDistribution(myScalarParameter)
})
nimbleCode({
   myScalarParameter ~ dnorm(0.0, 0.001)
   myData[1:numData] ~ dMyCustomDistribution(c(myScalarParameter))
})

This seems to work but seems... clunky.

nimbleCode({
   # Prior on the scalar parameter
   myScalarParameter ~ dnorm(0.0, 0.001)
   # Make a vectorised version of the parameter
   for(dataIter in 1:numData) {
      myVectorisedParameter[dataIter] <- myScalarParameter
   }
   # Likelihood calculation
   myData[1:numData] ~ dMyCustomDistribution(myVectorisedParameter[1:numData])
})

I could of course make another custom distribution for the use of scalar arguments but that also would result in lots of annoying code replication and seems inelegant.

I'm just wondering if I'm missing something obvious.  I can provide the specific code for my case if that helps but I think my question here is more conceptual than implementation-specific.

Thank you in advance for any help you can provide.

All the best,

Joe

messages.subject: Re: Promotion of scalars to length-1 vectors in nimbleCode
parts:
Thank you Perry and Daniel so much for your feedback.  Good to know that I wasn't just being silly and missing something obvious.

OK for now then it seems that I will stick to a minor variation of the solution in code snippet 4 in my original post.  From Perry's reply it seems that the vector needs to be of length greater than one to be truly accepted as a vector.  As my function recycles the parameter values to the desired length anyway then this will work for my code:

nimbleCode({
   # Prior on the scalar parameter

myScalarParameter[1] ~ dnorm(0.0, 0.001)
   # This only need to be length 2 as it just needs to be greater than one to trick NIMBLE into accepting
   # these arguments as a vector
   myScalarParameter[2] <- myScalarParameter[1]
   # Likelihood calculation (myScalarParameter gets recycled to the desired length internally in the distribution)
   myData[1:numData] ~ dMyCustomDistribution(myScalarParameter[1:2])
})

This only creates one extra logical node and that shouldn't slow things down too much.

Thank you both so much for your work on this.  I can imagine changing the underlying structure of NIMBLE to interpret scalars as 1-length vectors for functions that only accept vector input may cause a lot of headaches and may not even be desirable behaviour in many cases but a function/macro-like-thing that allows for the user to force this interpretation in particular cases (to allow for something like 'distributionWithVectorArg(Promote_To_Vector(aScalarVariable))') without having to create extra logical nodes would be super useful I think.

Hi Joe,

Thanks for this question.

Unfortunately, there are a variety of corners where nimble's hard typing creates limitations, and this is one of them.  It's something we hope to improve in a deeper renovation, although maybe we should try to do something superficial faster.

One possible workaround would be to always make the argument to dMyCustomDistribution be a vector by padding it with a dummy value if necessary.  E.g. 

myParameter[1] <- whatever_you_really_need
myParameter[2] <- 0 ## a dummy to make myParameter a true vector.

Then when you call dMyCustomDistribution, you could include an additional argument indicating whether myParameter is padded in this way.

Oh no, I just noticed that in the newly released nimble 0.6-12, there is a bug in the automatic creation of "r" functions for custom distributions (when the user doesn't provide the "r" function).  We added a new error trap for missing return() statements, and the dummy version of the "r" function now errors out for this reason.  Evidently we don't have that case in our test suite.  I'll go post an issue on github.
Perry

Alright, thanks! For now I've just got this in the model code and it's working (I also do this same control flow for priors, using either a multivariate normal or a regular normal for beta_abundance). Figured I'd post the code here in case it's a useful example for others.
    
    # negative binomial mean
    if (n_beta_abundance > 1) {
      mu_abundance[i] <-  
        (exp(x_abundance[i, 1:n_beta_abundance] %*% 
          beta_abundance[1:n_beta_abundance]))[1, 1] # [1, 1] is a hack to
                                                     # coerce to a scalar
    } else {
      mu_abundance[i] <-  
        (exp(x_abundance[i, 1] * 
               beta_abundance))
    }

One possible workaround would be to always make the argument to dMyCustomDistribution be a vector by padding it with a dummy value if necessary.  E.g. 

myParameter[1] <- whatever_you_really_need
myParameter[2] <- 0 ## a dummy to make myParameter a true vector.

Then when you call dMyCustomDistribution, you could include an additional argument indicating whether myParameter is padded in this way.

Oh no, I just noticed that in the newly released nimble 0.6-12, there is a bug in the automatic creation of "r" functions for custom distributions (when the user doesn't provide the "r" function).  We added a new error trap for missing return() statements, and the dummy version of the "r" function now errors out for this reason.  Evidently we don't have that case in our test suite.  I'll go post an issue on github.
